## Select outgoing acoustic and advected perturbations (`outflow`) {#sec-ch11-outflow}

### Summary

The outflow callback is the radiating boundary of the solver. It freezes the state the block was initialized
with, ghosts included, as the exterior background, and lets only the characteristics that leave the domain
carry information into the ghosts. Everything the callback needs beyond the tensor it fills travels in the
context: the EOS for the sound speed, the coordinate for the face-normal frame, and the two saved
backgrounds. The conserved-variable driver converts to primitives for it, and converts back with the dry
density as the tracer carrier.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Select outgoing perturbations; @eq-ch11-outflow-modes.

**Data.** Primitive state, EOS and saved background; SI[^rg-55087f577bc7] units listed below.

**Placement.** Physical fill; excluded from tangential corner refresh.

**Activation.** Set `outflow` on an external face; default off. `kScalar` and shallow-water inputs take the copy fallback.

**Guarantee / limits.** Joint admissibility scaling; no measured reflection result here.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test limits are in the Tests layer; solver ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

Local symbols, with appendix A, notation group 8a: $q_{\mathrm{bg}}$[^rg-598db203bccb] is the saved initial boundary background of a primitive $q$
(distinct from the well-balanced reference) and $\mathbf W_{\mathrm{bg}}$ the whole background; $d_q=q-q_{\mathrm{bg}}$ is the
interior perturbation of $q$, with $d_\rho$ [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$], $d_v$ [$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$] for the outward velocity and
$d_p$ [$\mathrm{Pa}$]; $Z=\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}c_{s,\mathrm{bg}}$ [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$] is the acoustic impedance and
$\alpha_{\mathrm{adm}}\in[0,1]$ the admissibility factor. New here: $v_{\mathrm{out}}$ the outward normal velocity
[$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$]; $\mathcal J_\pm=d_v\pm d_p/Z$ [$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$] the two acoustic mode amplitudes; and
$d_{\mathrm{ent}}=d_\rho-d_p/c_{s,\mathrm{bg}}^2$ [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$] the advected (entropy) combination.

### Derivation

Freeze an admissible background and an outward Cartesian face frame. For the outer $x_1$ face, write the frozen
material derivative as $\mathrm D/\mathrm Dt=\partial_t+v_{\mathrm{out},\mathrm{bg}}\partial_1$. The linearized mass, normal
momentum and pressure equations of the perturbation are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm Dd_\rho}{\mathrm Dt}&=-\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}\,\partial_1d_v,\\
\frac{\mathrm Dd_v}{\mathrm Dt}&=-\frac{1}{\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}}\,\partial_1d_p,\\
\frac{\mathrm Dd_p}{\mathrm Dt}&=-\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}c_{s,\mathrm{bg}}^2\,\partial_1d_v.
\end{aligned}
$$

Adding $\pm1/Z$ times the pressure equation to the momentum equation, and subtracting $1/c_{s,\mathrm{bg}}^2$ times the
pressure equation from the mass equation, decouples them into

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t\mathcal J_\pm+(v_{\mathrm{out},\mathrm{bg}}\pm c_{s,\mathrm{bg}})\,\partial_1\mathcal J_\pm&=0,\qquad
\mathcal J_\pm=d_v\pm d_p/Z,\quad Z=\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}c_{s,\mathrm{bg}},\\
\partial_t d_{\mathrm{ent}}+v_{\mathrm{out},\mathrm{bg}}\,\partial_1 d_{\mathrm{ent}}&=0,\qquad
d_{\mathrm{ent}}=d_\rho-d_p/c_{s,\mathrm{bg}}^2 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-outflow-modes}

The combinations of @eq-ch11-outflow-modes are formed by the tensors `plus`, `minus` and `entropy` of
`radiating` ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}), with `impedance` the background density times the
background sound speed `c0`; the same function inverts them below. Each is carried along its own speed, so at an
outer face $\mathcal J_+$ leaves the domain when $v_{\mathrm{out}}+c_s\ge0$, $\mathcal J_-$ when $v_{\mathrm{out}}-c_s\ge0$,
and $d_{\mathrm{ent}}$ when $v_{\mathrm{out}}\ge0$. A characteristic entering from outside has no interior-determined
perturbation: the boundary chooses zero perturbation for that incoming mode. The code uses the *current* outward
velocity and sound speed `c` of the nearest owned cell for this selector, while @eq-ch11-outflow-modes uses the
background impedance and sound speed. It is therefore a locally linear characteristic prescription, not the exact
nonlinear exterior solution.

Keep $\mathcal J_+$ when $v_{\mathrm{out}}+c_s\ge0$, keep $\mathcal J_-$ when $v_{\mathrm{out}}-c_s\ge0$, and otherwise set each
to zero. Keep $d_{\mathrm{ent}}$, the tangential velocities, the composition and the tracer-ratio perturbations when
$v_{\mathrm{out}}\ge0$; otherwise set them to zero. Equality selects the outgoing branch. Invert the split:

$$
\begin{aligned}
d_v&=(\mathcal J_++\mathcal J_-)/2,\\
d_p&=Z(\mathcal J_+-\mathcal J_-)/2,\\
d_\rho&=d_{\mathrm{ent}}+d_p/c_{s,\mathrm{bg}}^2.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-outflow-inverse}

`radiating` ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}) implements @eq-ch11-outflow-inverse by first
multiplying every row of the perturbation by the advection selector and then overwriting the normal
velocity, pressure and density rows with the inverted combinations. For the lower face the sign `sign`
reverses the coordinate normal before the split and again after the inversion, which accounts for the sign
in the velocity update. The same selected interior perturbation is supplied to every ghost, but each ghost
retains its own saved background.

For any lower-bounded component $q$ with floor $q_{\min}$, admissibility requires
$q_{\mathrm{bg}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{adm}}d_q\ge q_{\min}$.
If $d_q<0$, division gives the bound $(q_{\mathrm{bg}}-q_{\min})/(-d_q)$;
otherwise that component imposes no reduction. Start with one, take the minimum over all bounds, multiply
each binding bound below one by $0.99$, and clamp the result to $[0,1]$. Apply this to density with the EOS
density floor, pressure with the pressure floor, every $y_n$[^rg-ba8a61c1dc1e] with floor zero, the complement $1-\sum_n y_n$
with floor zero, and every passive tracer ratio $r_n$[^rg-7187b999100b] with floor zero. The nonnegative complement enforces
the composition sum. The same factor multiplies every perturbation, including the tracers:

$$
\mathbf W^{\mathrm{ghost}}=\mathbf W_{\mathrm{bg}}^{\mathrm{ghost}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{adm}}\,\mathbf d_{\mathbf W},
$$ {#eq-ch11-outflow-admissible}

with $\mathbf d_{\mathbf W}$ the selected perturbation of every primitive row.

The tensor `alpha` of `radiating` ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}) implements
@eq-ch11-outflow-admissible through the closure `lower`, which folds one bound at a time into the running
minimum. Convexity of these linear inequalities proves admissibility for an admissible background in exact
arithmetic. It proves neither a positive temperature for every EOS nor nonlinear nonreflection. Check C2
checks the invertible acoustic algebra; check C3 verifies the shared limiter against independent inequality
bounds, including a species-complement and a tracer-limited case [check
`src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.out`]. The checks
do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

`MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}})
clones the primitive state, ghosts included, into `boundary_reference_w` (and the scalar ratios into
`boundary_reference_r`) before the first physical fill, whenever `has_radiating_boundary`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::has_radiating_boundary >}}) finds an outflow callback on a
face with more than one cell and the EOS is not shallow water. The callback first takes the scalar and
shallow-water fallback, then requires the EOS, the coordinate and a saved background of the same shape as
its input, a supported EOS type, primitive input, finite input, and an admissible background
(`check_background`, {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp check_background >}}: finite, density and pressure at or
above their floors, nonnegative composition summing to at most one); it also requires a finite positive sound
speed of the background over the whole source plane (the layer of cells next to the face) and of the current state
over the cells of that plane that belong to the block interior. A cell of the plane outside the interior, in another
direction's ghost rows, may hold a stale or forced state that the exchange or the next face overwrites; where its
sound speed is not finite and positive it takes the background state and the background sound speed
(`in_plane`, {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}). It transforms both states to the face frame with the
coordinate's `boundary_velocity_`, forms the perturbation from the nearest owned cell, selects the outgoing
modes, limits each ghost, transforms back, and writes only the ghosts; with tracers it also writes the
tracer-ratio ghosts as background plus `alpha` times the selected ratio perturbation.

Conserved calls go through `MeshBlockImpl::apply_boundaries`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_boundaries >}}): consecutive outflow faces share one
primitive conversion of the block and are recorded as pending; before any other callback runs, and at the
end, the pending ghost slabs are converted back and copied into the conserved tensor. The tracer densities
written back are the ratios times the conserved dry density, as in the scalar primitive conversion, not the
primitive total density. The cartoon shows the mode directions and the convex contraction separately. No
coupled wall/seam convergence or reflection measurement is reported here.

### Code

**How to use.** Initialize admissible hydro values in owned cells and ghosts before block initialization captures
the background. Include nonnegative tracer ratios when transporting tracers. Use `apply_boundaries` to prepare
primitives; the saved background must survive a restart.

This is a configuration fragment, not a standalone simulation deck.

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `forcing`[^rg-c2adbe6bd0b3], `const-gravity`[^rg-07ad360aab23], `gravity-work-fixer`[^rg-33815445b671].
```yaml
boundary-condition:
  external:
    x1-inner: outflow
    x1-outer: outflow
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    gravity-work-fixer: false
```

**Refusals and prerequisites.** `radiating` refuses missing context with "outflow requires EOS, coordinate and
saved initial background" and unsupported EOS types with "Unsupported outflow EOS: ". It refuses a direct
non-primitive call with "outflow: prepare primitive context with apply_boundaries". Shape mismatch, nonfinite
inputs and invalid background density, pressure or composition are also checked there. Set
`forcing/const-gravity/gravity-work-fixer` to `false` to avoid using a closed-column energy correction on open x1 faces.

**Read the implementation.** `radiating` ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}) contains:

```cpp
auto plus = torch::where(un + c >= 0, sign * d[vn] + d[IPR] / impedance, 0.);
auto minus = torch::where(un - c >= 0, sign * d[vn] - d[IPR] / impedance, 0.);
auto entropy = torch::where(advect, d[IDN] - d[IPR] / c0.square(), 0.);
```

`plus`, `minus` and `entropy` are the selected $\mathcal J_+$, $\mathcal J_-$ and $d_{\mathrm{ent}}$ of @eq-ch11-outflow-modes. The following inverse gives @eq-ch11-outflow-inverse; the shared limiter gives @eq-ch11-outflow-admissible.

| detect | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::has_radiating_boundary >}} | `has_radiating_boundary` | `outflow` |
| background | {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp check_background >}} | `check_background` | `outflow` |
| radiating | {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}} | `radiating` | `outflow` |

: Implementation sites for outflow. {#tbl-ch11-outflow-code}

1. Take the scalar/shallow-water fallback first; otherwise require the EOS, the coordinate and a saved
   same-shape background. The anchor `radiating` is in {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}.
2. Require a supported EOS, primitive input, finite input, positive finite sound speeds (the background's on the
   whole source plane, the current state's on its interior cells, the background substituted elsewhere), and an
   admissible background density, pressure and composition. The anchor `check_background` is in
   {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp check_background >}}.
3. Split in the face frame, select the modes with the current speeds, and reconstruct the selected
   perturbation. The anchor `plus` is in {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}.
4. Validate the tracer background's shape, finiteness and nonnegativity; reduce the shared factor and verify
   that the reconstructed ghosts are finite. The anchor `alpha` is in {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}.
5. Flush the pending conserved faces in face order with the dry-density tracer conversion. The anchor
   `apply_boundaries` is in {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_boundaries >}}.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Outflow is skipped by the tangential corner refresh
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}). The gravity-work fixer is not an
open-boundary energy budget: `MeshBlockImpl::apply_gravity_work_fixer`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_gravity_work_fixer >}}) refuses a step in which more
than a round-off bound of mass crossed an x1 wall face, and the error text directs the user to
`gravity-work-fixer: false` for open x1 boundaries. The implicit closure of @sec-ch11-solids stays
reflecting at the column ends, so a characteristic ghost fill does not establish a characteristic implicit
boundary. Saved backgrounds are fixed initialization data; no adaptive exterior evolution is implemented by
this callback.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::

[^rg-55087f577bc7]: SI — International System of Units; notation only; see @sec-appa

[^rg-598db203bccb]: $q_{\mathrm{bg}}$ — the saved background value of a primitive $q$ at a radiating boundary

[^rg-ba8a61c1dc1e]: $y_n$ — mass fraction of species $n$ **per unit total mass**, $\rho_n = \rho y_n$, dimensionless [-]; this is snapy's composition variable and the only one the state vector carries

[^rg-7187b999100b]: $r_n$ — mass mixing ratio of species $n$ **per unit dry mass**, $r_n = \rho_n/\rho_{\mathrm{d}}$, dimensionless [-]; used only where the code is per dry air (passive tracers, @sec-ch10-tracer). Never written $r$ without its species subscript, because $r$ alone is the radius (§1)

[^rg-c2adbe6bd0b3]: forcing — forcing options block: a map with one sub-block per forcing component

[^rg-07ad360aab23]: const-gravity — constant-gravity forcing component

[^rg-33815445b671]: gravity-work-fixer — whether the gravity-work fixer runs (a boolean; default true with `gravity-work: cell`, and it needs `cell`)

[^rg-94bb6a1dab2d]: PLM — piecewise-linear method

[^rg-aeddec0575d5]: WENO5 — fifth-order weighted essentially non-oscillatory reconstruction
